chapters.1.lds: Which tribes drive out their neighbors? Which leave them in place or force them to work?
chapters.4.meaning: Deborah directs Barak, and Jael kills Sisera. Both women shape the battle’s outcome.
chapters.5.summary: Deborah and Barak sing about the battle. They praise willing tribes and Jael. Sisera’s mother waits for him to return.
chapters.7.meaning: God reduces Gideon’s army before the battle. Israel must not claim that its own strength won.
chapters.8.meaning: Gideon refuses to become king. Yet the gold ephod he makes leads the people away from God.
chapters.10.meaning: Israel again worships other gods and suffers attack. Its plea for help leads into Jephthah’s story.
chapters.11.meaning: Jephthah promises a burnt offering before battle. His daughter meets him first when he returns.
chapters.11.lds: The older manual reads the vow as lifelong service. Hayes reads it as sacrifice. The readings differ over the daughter’s fate.
chapters.14.meaning: Men threaten to burn Samson’s wife and her family. Fear leads her to reveal his riddle.
chapters.16.meaning: Delilah learns Samson’s secret and helps his enemies capture him. Samson’s final act kills himself and many others.
chapters.18.meaning: Dan’s armed men take Micah’s priest and worship objects. They destroy the peaceful town of Laish.
people.joseph.meaning: Joseph’s tribes attack Bethel in the opening chapter. A local man shows them its entrance.
people.judah.meaning: Judah’s tribe begins the battles after Joshua’s death. It calls on Simeon for help.
people.reuben.meaning: Deborah’s song questions why Reuben’s groups stayed with their flocks instead of helping.
people.simeon.meaning: Simeon’s tribe helps Judah fight. Judah then helps Simeon in return.
people.levi.meaning: Levi’s name identifies the priestly tribe. The book follows two later men from this tribe.
people.benjamin.meaning: Benjamin’s tribe leaves Jebusites in Jerusalem. Its defense of Gibeah later brings war with Israel.
people.ephraim.meaning: Ephraim’s men join battles but also dispute other leaders’ choices. Their quarrel with Jephthah ends in killing.
people.manasseh.meaning: Manasseh’s tribe leaves some Canaanite towns in place. Gideon later comes from one of its families.
people.zebulun.meaning: Zebulun’s people risk their lives in the battle celebrated by Deborah’s song.
people.issachar.meaning: Issachar’s leaders stand with Deborah. The song praises their part in the battle.
people.dan.meaning: Dan’s tribe seeks new land and takes Laish. The new town also takes Dan’s name.
people.naphtali.meaning: Barak gathers men from Naphtali and Zebulun to fight Sisera’s army.
people.gad.meaning: Gad’s descendants belong to the tribes east of the Jordan. Gad himself lived before these events.
people.asher.meaning: Deborah’s song asks why Asher stayed near the coast during the battle.
people.cushan-rishathaim.meaning: Cushan Rishathaim rules over Israel for eight years. Othniel leads Israel to freedom.
people.jabin-judges.meaning: Jabin rules at Hazor and oppresses Israel. Sisera commands his army.
people.gideon.meaning: Gideon seeks signs before leading Israel. After victory, his revenge and gold ephod bring further harm.
people.oreb.meaning: Ephraim’s men kill Oreb during the pursuit. The rock where he dies bears his name.
people.zeeb.meaning: Ephraim’s men kill Zeeb at a winepress during the pursuit.
people.zalmunna.meaning: Gideon pursues Zalmunna and Zebah across the Jordan. They had killed Gideon’s brothers.
people.tola.meaning: Tola leads Israel for twenty-three years. He lives and is buried at Shamir.
people.jair.meaning: Jair leads Israel for twenty-two years. His thirty sons ride donkeys and hold thirty towns.
people.jephthah.meaning: Jephthah returns from exile to lead Gilead’s forces. His vow brings tragedy to his only child.
people.abdon.meaning: Abdon’s many sons and grandsons ride donkeys. The notice shows his family’s wealth and standing.
people.delilah.meaning: Delilah repeatedly asks how Samson can be bound. She gives his secret to the Philistine rulers.
people.jonathan-priest.meaning: Jonathan accepts work as Dan’s priest. Old copies differ over whether his ancestor’s name is Moses or Manasseh.
